title: Tesla Ends Cybertruck Production, Pivots Factory to Cybercab Robotaxi
summary: Tesla ends Cybertruck production by mid-2027, pivoting its Texas factory to the Cybercab robotaxi. Sales dropped 48% in 2025 with 11 recalls since launch. What builders need to know about Tesla's autonomy bet.

Cybertruck Discontinued


# Tesla Ends Cybertruck Production, Pivots Factory to Cybercab Robotaxi


By OpenTools Team


·


November 11, 2026


Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production by mid‑2027, freeing its Texas Gigafactory for the Cybercab robotaxi. The angular pickup sold just 20,237 units in 2025 — down 48% from 2024 and a fraction of Musk's original 250,000/year target. The move marks the end of one of tech's most controversial products and a hard pivot toward autonomy.


## The End of the Road for Tesla's Most Controversial Vehicle


Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas Gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk confirmed, ending one of the most polarizing product runs in automotive history. The factory — the only facility equipped to manufacture the truck's unique stainless steel body — will shift capacity to the **Cybercab robotaxi** , according to[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-wind-down-cybertruck-production-texas-gigafactory-next-year-musk-says-2026-11-06/) .


Musk called the Cybertruck "the best vehicle Tesla has ever made" and described the wind-down as "the end of an era" in a post on X. Tesla has not confirmed whether production will move elsewhere or be phased out entirely, but the Austin plant's specialized tooling makes relocation unlikely.


## Sales Never Came Close to the 250,000 Target


Tesla sold **20,237 Cybertrucks in 2025** , down 48% from 38,965 in 2024, according to[Kelley Blue Book data reported by CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/tesla-ending-cybertruck-production-next-year/) . That's a fraction of Musk's original target of 250,000 units per year, stated when commercial production began in 2023.


Even SpaceX — Musk's own company — was one of the largest buyers, purchasing **$131 million worth of Cybertrucks** at list price in 2025, as disclosed in SpaceX's IPO filing[per Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-wind-down-cybertruck-production-texas-gigafactory-next-year-musk-says-2026-11-06/) . In an ironic twist, Musk acknowledged the backlog of orders exceeds what Tesla can produce before the line shuts down, meaning some deposit-holders will get refunds rather than trucks.


The Cybertruck had its best sales month in over a year in October 2026 with 1,914 units sold, as reported by[Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/11/10/tesla-cybertruck-had-its-best-month-in-over-a-year-its-still-going-away/) — but it wasn't enough to change the trajectory.


## 11 Recalls and a Design That Couldn't Cross Borders


The Cybertruck faced **11 federal safety recalls** since deliveries began in late 2023, according to NHTSA data cited by[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-wind-down-cybertruck-production-texas-gigafactory-next-year-musk-says-2026-11-06/) . Issues ranged from dangerously faulty accelerator pedal pads to incorrect adhesive causing body panels to potentially detach at highway speeds.


The angular stainless steel design that made the truck distinctive also made it **effectively banned in the European Union and UK** due to pedestrian-impact crash regulations, as documented by[WIRED](https://www.wired.com/video/watch/end-of-an-error-elon-musk-finally-puts-cybertruck-out-of-its-misery) . Tesla separately cancelled Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand because no right-hand-drive version was ever built. Former Aston Martin CEO Andy Palmer told[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-wind-down-cybertruck-production-texas-gigafactory-next-year-musk-says-2026-11-06/) : "Anywhere where you have crash regulation that takes into account pedestrian impact, that Cybertruck won't go, can't go."


Even in the US market, electric pickups have broadly struggled. Automotive analyst Felipe Munoz told[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-wind-down-cybertruck-production-texas-gigafactory-next-year-musk-says-2026-11-06/) : "All of them lost the competition because electric pickups aren't popular in the US."


## The Cybercab Pivot: No Steering Wheel, No Pedals


The Texas Gigafactory's freed capacity will go to the **Cybercab** , Tesla's fully autonomous robotaxi with butterfly doors and no steering wheel, pedals, or mirrors. A small fleet has been operating in Austin since September 2026, with about 570 of 1,200 Tesla robotaxis in Texas being Cybercabs,[per Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-wind-down-cybertruck-production-texas-gigafactory-next-year-musk-says-2026-11-06/) .


Installed Cybercab production capacity already exceeds 125,000 units. Wes Morrill, the Cybertruck lead engineer, wrote on X: "Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab."


Wall Street analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co told[CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/tesla-ending-cybertruck-production-next-year/) that "the writing was on the wall" for the Cybertruck and that "Musk is focused on robotics and the robotaxi era." Ives also predicted Tesla could be acquired by SpaceX next year, giving the EV company more capital.


## NHTSA Opens Audit of Cybercab Self-Certification


The pivot isn't without regulatory risk. The **NHTSA opened an audit in September 2026** to review Tesla's self-certification of Cybercab compliance with federal safety standards,[Reuters reports](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-wind-down-cybertruck-production-texas-gigafactory-next-year-musk-says-2026-11-06/) . A vehicle with no steering wheel or mirrors falls outside conventional safety frameworks, and the audit could delay broader deployment.


Tesla's overall EV business remains strong — Model Y and Model 3[continue](https://opentools.ai/tools/continue) to dominate sales. But the Cybertruck's failure highlights the gap between Musk's grand pronouncements and market reality. Palmer told[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-wind-down-cybertruck-production-texas-gigafactory-next-year-musk-says-2026-11-06/) : "It doesn't make sense to keep it going when it's not meeting its targets. Every rational auto guy would say the same."


## What This Signals for Tesla's Strategy


The Cybertruck wind-down is the clearest signal yet that Tesla is reorganizing around **autonomy and AI** , not traditional vehicle manufacturing. The company that once promised to reinvent the pickup truck is now betting its future on a robotaxi network.


The transition carries real risk: the Cybercab faces unresolved safety audits, robotaxi economics remain unproven at scale, and Elon Musk's recent political spending — nearly $500 million on midterm elections where his candidates largely lost — has created distractions, with[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-wind-down-cybertruck-production-texas-gigafactory-next-year-musk-says-2026-11-06/) noting that combined Musk companies were on track to lose more than $180 billion in market cap for the week of the midterms.


For builders and developers, the Cybercab platform may eventually offer API access for autonomous fleet management — but for now, the takeaway is simpler: Tesla is killing its most distinctive product to chase a much bigger, and much riskier, autonomous future.
